This is because PROE reflects structural dominance—how much a team outperforms expectations given its formation or strategy—while EPA/play measures actual performance per play. When these two metrics diverge, it suggests that structural factors (like 2-high shells) are forcing outcomes rather than aggressive play. The GSE simulation isolates this by modeling 175-snap sequences, showing that such profiles cluster in predictable formations. The separation of EPA/play only emerges when filtering by game context (e.g., 3rd-and-long vs 1st), suggesting that tactical behavior is not uniform but context-sensitive. This reveals a duality in how teams can be efficient without being aggressive, and how structural design can override individual performance metrics.
